{
  "need": "Status",
  "secondary": { "name": "Competence", "description": "If they did do it, they need that genuine capability recognized; if they didn't, they're likely hiding a belief that their real work isn't good enough." },
  "read": "Whether this is a leap or a lift from somewhere else, the student's sense of mattering is at the center. A student who grew fast needs to know you see the real them, not a fluke. A student who borrowed someone else's work is probably telling you their own effort feels too risky to show — that their authentic work won't be respected.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Lead with suspicion — ask pointed questions or run it through a detector right away — which signals you assume the worst and shuts down any chance they'll tell you the truth." },
  "mentorMove": "Go in curious, not accusatory. Treat this as a chance to understand their thinking process, which surfaces the truth naturally and keeps the relationship intact whether they grew or they didn't.",
  "holdFirm": ["The work has to be theirs — that standard doesn't move.", "They need to be able to walk you through it, not just hand it in."],
  "stayFlexible": ["How you surface that — a quick conversation, a few follow-up questions on the piece, a short in-class extension — can flex to what feels least humiliating.", "If it turns out they did do it, find a way to make that growth visible and public in some small way."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I read your piece and honestly it stopped me. That doesn't happen every day." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "I want to hear you talk through it a little — where did the idea for this section come from? Walk me through what you were thinking when you put this part together." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here's what I'm going to do: I want to give you a chance to show me this thinking is yours, because if it is, you deserve real credit for it — not just a grade, but actual recognition that something shifted for you. So let's spend two minutes on it right now." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I'm holding you to a high bar here because I think you can clear it — and I mean that. Whatever happened with this piece, I want to help you get to the point where work this strong is something you know came from you. That's worth more than any single assignment." }
  ],
  "longGame": "If the conversation reveals growth, name it specifically and often — students who finally break through need to hear it reflected back until they own it. If it reveals something else, treat it as data about what they believe their real work is worth, and start building their confidence in showing you the unpolished version."
}
situation: A student handed in work far better than anything they have produced before, and I genuinely cannot tell if it is a breakthrough or if someone else did it.
